sec: Conn's syndrome: classification and pathophysiology · p841

items.q: The acquired forms account for what share of primary hyperaldosteronism (PHA)?
items.exp: PHA is 90% acquired and 10% familial. (Book p841)

items.q: Match the acquired PHA cause to its frequency — 1) B/L adrenal micronodular hyperplasia  2) U/L adrenal adenoma … A) 30%  B) 60%
items.exp: Bilateral micronodular hyperplasia is 60%; unilateral adrenal adenoma (Conn's syndrome) is 30%. (Book p841)
U/L adrenal adenoma (30%) is a.k.a. Conn's syndrome. (Book p841)

items.q: Match familial PHA — 1) Type I  2) Type II … A) ClCN2 mutation  B) Glucocorticoid remediable aldosteronism (GRA), autosomal dominant
items.exp: Familial (10%): Type I = GRA (AD); Type II = ClCN2 mutation. (Book p841)

items.q: In the cortical collecting duct P-cell, aldosterone acts via MR to induce AIP, which then activates:
items.exp: MR–Aldo (+) induces AIP (aldosterone-induced protein) which (+) activates ENaC, retaining Na+ and losing K+/H+. (Book p841)

items.q: AIP in the P-cell diagram stands for ___.
Despite salt and water retention, PHA causes no edema because:
opts: The retained volume stimulates ANP (atrial natriuretic peptide)
The kidney escapes via pressure natriuresis of the proximal tubule only
items.exp: Salt & water retention stimulates ANP, so there is no edema. (Book p841)

items.q: The classic triad of PHA is hypertension with:
items.exp: Triad: HTN, hypokalaemia, metabolic alkalosis. (Book p841)

items.q: In PHA-associated hypertension, the book notes:
items.exp: The hypertension shows diastolic > systolic. (Book p841)

items.q: Match AME vs GRA — 1) AME inheritance  2) GRA inheritance  3) AME cause  4) GRA cause … A) Autosomal dominant  B) Autosomal recessive  C) 11β-HSD2 defect  D) Chimeric ACTH-driven aldosterone secretion
items.exp: AME is AR with 11β-HSD2 defect; GRA is AD with a chimeric effect where ACTH drives aldosterone. Both give HTN + mA + hypokalaemia. (Book p841)

items.q: ‘GRA is treated with steroids, which suppress the ACTH driving the aldosterone.’
items.exp: Rx steroids (−) suppress ACTH and hence the chimeric aldosterone secretion in GRA. (Book p841)
